Figure 2:Overview ofeDMDon a 2D tree-structured toy distribution (gray).Left: a 4-step student denoises from noise (σ=1\sigma=1) to its final output (σ=0\sigma=0, “delivered”); each update noises one step’s prediction to a levelτ\tau(green bar: its range) and compares the teacher and the fake model at the resulting query𝐲\mathbf{y}.
Right: compared with DMD2 and TDM,eDMDtrains the fake model on final outputs only (top), draws the queries of intermediate steps from a calibrated density (middle; ticks: the level each step denoises to), and answers low-noise queries with a multi-step teacher instead of a single prediction (bottom; percentages: answers on the tree).

Figure 3:Intermediate-based references deflect the update from the desired direction; the endpoint reference does not.Each row shows one reference (mixture, stage, endpoint): what the fake model learns (left) and one update of the final outputs for a student with mismatched (q≠pq\neq p, middle) and matched (q=pq=p, right) final outputs.
Gray arrows show the desired update,i.e., the endpoint matching termDp−DqD_{p}-D_{q}ofEq.3, which is zero for the matched student; colored arrows show the additional displacement caused by the reference residual (numbers: mean norms).

Figure 4:Qualitative results on FLUX.2-klein-4B.Leftmost: teacher (50 steps,w=4w=4); others: 4-step students at the checkpoints ofTab.1; shared prompt and noise per row.
Best viewed zoomed in: on fine structures such as fur, hair, and grass,eDMDpreserves richer details and fewer artifacts, yielding more natural textures than existing methods.

Figure A.1:Opposite updates despite correct final outputs.Each pair hasq=pq=pbut opposite intermediate biases, shown in the top three rows: clean predictions (DMD2, left) or landing states (TDM, right).
Gray backgrounds show the teacher; dots are student samples, colored by relative density (blue: below the teacher; red: above).
Bottom: updates induced by the reference residual (numbers: mean norms); the endpoint reference gives zero update.
ED: energy distance (lower is better).

Figure A.2:The endpoint reference improves imperfect students and preserves matched outputs.Top: a consistency student starts with blurred outputs; bottom: an Euler student starts atq=pq=p.
Left: final output energy distance (lower is better; smoothed geometric mean and range over three seeds).
Right: seed-0 samples before and after 1,500 iterations with the baseline or endpoint reference. Gray: teacher; black dots: student.
